source_text: 1. Quon1am igitur in hoe mundo quidam quidem accurrunt lumini, et per fidem uniunt se Deo; alii autem absistunt a lumine, et separant seipsos a Deo: venit Verbum Dei, omnibus aptam habitationem inferens ; his quidem qui in lumine sunt, ut fruantur eo, et his quee in eo sunt bonis: his autem qui in tenebris sunt, ut participentur eas calamitates quze in eis sunt. Et propter hoe ait, hos quidem qui sunt ad dexteram vocari in regnum Patris: autem qui sunt a sinistra in eternum ignem missurum, Semetipsos enim omnibus privaverunt bonis, 2. Et propter hoe Apostolus ait: Pro eo quod dilectionem Dei non receperunt, ut salvi ferent, et ideo mittet eis Deus operationem erroris, ut credant mendacio, ut judicentur omnes qui non crediderunt veritati, sed consenserunt iniquitati : illo enim veniente, et sua sententia apostasiam recapitulante in semetipsum, et sua voluntate et arbitrio operante quaecunque operabitur, et in templo Dei sedente, ut sicut Christum adorent illum qui seducentur ab quapropter et juste in stagnum projicietur ignis ; Deo autem secundum suam providentiam preesciente omnia, et apto tempore eum qui talis futurus erat immittente, wt credant falso, ut judicentur omnes qui non crediderunt veritati, sed consenserunt iniquitati. Cujus adventum Johannes in Apocalypsi significavit ita: Et bestia quam videram, similis erat pardo, et pedes ejus quasi ursi, et os ejus quasi os leonis; et dedit ei draco virtutem suam, et thronum suum, et potestatem magnam; et unum ew capitibus ejus’ quasi occisum in mortem, e plaga mortis ejus curata est, et admirata est universa terra post bestiam: et adoraverunt draconem, 4 quoniam dedit potestatem bestie ; et adoraverunt bestiam dicentes: Quis similis bestice illi, et quis potest pugnare cum ipsa? Et datum est e os loquens magna et blasphemiam, et data est ei potestas mensibus xu. et ®duobus. Et aperuit os swum ad blasphemium adversus Deum, blasphemare nomen ejus, et tabernaculum ejus, et eos qui in colo habitant, Ht data est ei potestas super omnem tribum, et populum, et linguam, et gentem. Et adoraverunt eum omnes qui habitant super terram, cujus non est scriptum nomen in libro vitee Agni occisi a constitutione mundi. Si quis habet aures, audiat. Si quis in captivitatem duxerit, in captivitatem ibit. Si quis gladio occioportet eum in gladio occidi. Hic est sustinentia et fides sanctorum. Post deinde et de armigero ejus, quem et pseudoprophetam vocat : Loguebatur, inquit, quasi draco, et potestatem prime bestice omnem faciebat in conspectu aus : et facit terram, et qui habitant in ea, ut adorarent bestiam primam, cujus curata est plaga mortis ejus. Et faciet signa magna, ut e ignem faciat de celo descendere in terram in conspectu hominum ; et seducet inhabitantes super terram, Heee ne quis eum divina virtute putet signa facere, sed magica operatione. Et non est mirandum, si deemoniis et apostaticis spiritibus ministrantibus ei, per eos faciat signa, in seducat habitantes super terram. Et imaginem, ait, Jubebit fiers bestiae, et spiritum dabit imagini, uti et loquatur imago, et eos qui non adoraverint eam faciet occidi. Et characterem autem, ait, in fronte, et in manu dextra faciet dari, ne possit aliquis emere vel vendere, nisi qui habet characterem nominis bestia, vel numerum nominis ejus: et esse numerum sexcentos sexaginta sew, quod est, sexies centeni, et deni sewies, et singulares sex; im universze apostasize ejus, quze facta est in sex millibus annorum. 8. Quotquot enim diebus hic factus est mundus, tot et millenis annis consummatur. Et propter hoe ait Scriptura Et consummata sunt celum et terra, et omnis ornatus ecorum. consummavit Deus die sexto omnia opera sua que fecit, et requievit in die septimo ab omnibus operibus suis que fecit. Hoe autem est et antefactorum narratio, quemadmodum facta sunt, et futurorum prophetia. Etenim dies Domini quasi mille anni; in sex autem diebus consummata sunt que facta sunt: manifestum est quoniam consummatio ipsorum sextus millesimus annus est. Et propter hoc in omni tempore, plasmatus initio homo per manus Dei, id est, Filii et Spiritus, fit secundum imaginem et similitudinem Dei, paleis quidem abjectis, quee sunt apostasia ; frumento autem in horreum assumto, quod est hi qui ad Deum fide fructificant. Et propterea tribulatio necessaria est his qui salvantur, ut quodammodo contriti, et attenuati, et conspersi per patientiam Verbo Dei, et igniti, apti sint ad convivium Regis. Quemadmodum quidam de nostris dixit, propter martyrium in Deum adjudicatus ad bestias: Quoniam frumentum sum Christi, et per dentes bestiarum molor, ut mundus panis Dei inveniar. Universa ad utilitatem hominum facta esse: et de Antichristi dolis, nequitia, vi apostatica a diluvio, et deinceps in Ananie, Azarie et Misaelis persecutione, prafigurata.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore, since in this world some indeed run to the light and through faith unite themselves to God, but others withdraw from the light and separate themselves from God: the Word of God comes, bringing a suitable dwelling for all; for those who are in the light, so that they may enjoy it and the goods that are in it; but for those who are in darkness, so that they may participate in the calamities that are in them. And because of this, it says that those who are on the right are called into the kingdom of the Father, but those who are on the left are sent into eternal fire. For they have deprived themselves of all goods. And because of this, the Apostle says: Since they did not receive the love of God, so that they might be saved, and therefore God will send them a working of error, so that they may believe a lie, so that all who did not believe the truth but consented to iniquity may be judged. For when he comes, and with his own judgment recapitulates the apostasy in himself, and with his own will and decision operates whatever he operates, and sitting in the temple of God, so that those who are seduced by him may adore him as Christ; therefore, they will be justly thrown into the lake of fire. But God, according to his own providence, foreknowing all things, and at the suitable time sending him who was to be such, so that they may believe a falsehood, so that all who did not believe the truth but consented to iniquity may be judged. The coming of whom John signified in the Apocalypse thus: And the beast that I saw was similar to a leopard, and its feet were like those of a bear, and its mouth was like the mouth of a lion; and the dragon gave it its power, and its throne, and great authority; and one of its heads was as if slain to death, and the wound of its death was healed, and the whole earth was amazed after the beast; and they worshiped the dragon, because it gave authority to the beast; and they worshiped the beast, saying: Who is similar to the beast, and who can fight with it? And a mouth speaking great things and blasphemies was given to it, and authority was given to it for forty-two months. And it opened its mouth to blasphemy against God, to blaspheme his name, and his tabernacle, and those who dwell in heaven. And authority was given to it over every tribe, and people, and language, and nation. And all who dwell on the earth worshiped it, whose name is not written in the book of life of the slain Lamb from the foundation of the world. If anyone has ears, let him hear. If anyone is to be taken captive, he will be taken captive; if anyone is to be slain with the sword, he must be slain with the sword. This is the patience and faith of the saints. After this, also about his armor-bearer, whom he also calls a false prophet: It spoke, he says, like a dragon, and it did all the power of the first beast in the sight of men; and it makes the earth and those who dwell in it worship the first beast, whose wound of death was healed. And it will do great signs, so that it even makes fire come down from heaven to earth in the sight of men; and it will seduce the inhabitants of the earth, so that they may not think that he does signs by divine power, but by magical operation. And it is not to be wondered at, if with the help of demons and apostate spirits ministering to him, he does signs, and seduces the inhabitants of the earth. And an image, he says, it will make of the beast, and it will give spirit to the image, so that the image may even speak, and it will make those who do not worship it be killed. And a mark, he says, will be given on the forehead and on the right hand, so that no one may be able to buy or sell, except him who has the mark of the name of the beast, or the number of its name: and the number is six hundred sixty-six, which is, six times one hundred, and ten, and seven, and six; in all the apostasy of it, which was made in six thousand years. For as many days as the world was made, so many thousand years it is completed. And because of this, Scripture says: And heaven and earth and all their adornment were completed. God completed all his works that he made on the sixth day, and he rested on the seventh day from all his works that he made. But this is also a narrative of past things, and a prophecy of future things. For the day of the Lord is like a thousand years; but in six days the things that were made were completed: it is clear that the completion of them is the sixth thousandth year. And because of this, in every time, man, formed at the beginning by the hands of God, that is, by the Son and the Spirit, is made according to the image and likeness of God, casting away the chaff, which are the apostasies; but gathering the wheat into the storehouse, which are those who bear fruit in faith to God. And therefore, tribulation is necessary for those who are saved, so that, being somehow broken, and attenuated, and sprinkled with patience, with the Word of God, and ignited, they may be fit for the banquet of the King. As one of ours said, who was condemned to the beasts for the testimony of God: For I am the grain of Christ, and I am ground by the teeth of the beasts, so that I may be found as the pure bread of God. All things were made for the utility of men: and about the snares of the Antichrist, and his wickedness, and apostatic power from the flood, and from then on in the persecution of Ananias, Azarias, and Misael, prefigured.

pass_b_english: In this world some run toward the light and, through faith, join themselves to God, while others turn away from the light and separate themselves from him. The Word of God comes bringing a dwelling suited to everyone: for those who are in the light, that they may enjoy it and the good things within it; for those who are in darkness, that they may share in the calamities that belong to them. Therefore he says that those on the right are called into the kingdom of the Father, but those on the left are sent into eternal fire, because they have deprived themselves of every good (Matt 25:34, 41).

For this reason the Apostle declares: because they did not receive the love of God so as to be saved, God will send them a working of error, so that they believe a lie, so that all who did not believe the truth but consented to iniquity may be judged (2 Thess 2:10-12). When that one comes, he will recapitulate the apostasy in himself by his own sentence, and by his own will and choice he will do whatever he does, and he will sit in the temple of God so that those he deceives may worship him as Christ; therefore they will justly be thrown into the lake of fire (2 Thess 2:4; Rev 19:20). Yet God, according to his providence, foreknows all things and at the fitting time sends the one who is to be such a person, so that they may believe falsehood, so that all who did not believe the truth but consented to iniquity may be judged.

John signified his coming in the Apocalypse: the beast I saw was like a leopard, its feet were like a bear's, and its mouth like a lion's mouth; the dragon gave it his power, his throne, and great authority (Rev 13:1-2). One of its heads seemed to have been slain to death, but its death wound was healed, and the whole earth marveled and followed the beast; they worshiped the dragon because he had given authority to the beast, and they worshiped the beast, saying, 'Who is like the beast, and who can fight against it?' (Rev 13:3-4). A mouth speaking great things and blasphemies was given to it, and authority to act for forty-two months (Rev 13:5). It opened its mouth to blaspheme God, to blaspheme his name and his dwelling place, and those who dwell in heaven (Rev 13:6). Authority was given it over every tribe, people, language, and nation, and all who dwell on the earth worshiped it—everyone whose name has not been written from the foundation of the world in the book of life of the Lamb who was slain (Rev 13:7-8). If anyone has an ear, let him hear. If anyone is to be taken captive, to captivity he goes; if anyone is to be killed with the sword, with the sword he must be killed. Here is the endurance and faith of the saints (Rev 13:9-10).

Then I saw another beast rising out of the earth, the one he calls the false prophet. It spoke like a dragon and exercised all the authority of the first beast in its presence, and it made the earth and its inhabitants worship the first beast, whose death wound had been healed (Rev 13:11-12). It performs great signs, even making fire come down from heaven to earth before people, and by these signs it deceives the inhabitants of the earth (Rev 13:13-14). No one should think it does these signs by divine power, but by magical operation; it is no wonder, since demons and apostate spirits serve it and through them it performs signs and deceives the earth's inhabitants (Rev 13:14; 16:13-14). It will order an image of the beast to be made, give breath to the image so that it can speak, and cause all who refuse to worship the image to be killed (Rev 13:15). It will also cause a mark to be put on the right hand or forehead of everyone, so that no one can buy or sell unless they have the mark, that is, the name of the beast or the number of its name (Rev 13:16-17). The number is six hundred sixty-six: six times one hundred, plus ten times seven, plus six; this sums up the whole apostasy that has taken place over six thousand years (Rev 13:18).

For as many days as the world was made, so many thousands of years it will be completed. Therefore Scripture says: 'And the heavens and the earth were finished, and all their host. And on the sixth day God finished his work that he had done, and he rested on the seventh day from all his work that he had done' (Gen 2:1-2). This is both a narrative of past things and a prophecy of future things. For the day of the Lord is like a thousand years (Ps 90:4); in six days the things that were made were finished, so it is clear that their completion comes in the sixth thousandth year.

For this reason, at every time the human being, formed at the beginning by the hands of God—that is, by the Son and the Spirit—is made according to the image and likeness of God, casting away the chaff, which are the apostasies, but gathering the wheat into the storehouse, which are those who bear fruit in faith toward God (Matt 3:12). Therefore tribulation is necessary for those who are saved, so that—being in a sense broken, refined, and sprinkled with patience by the Word of God, and kindled—they may become fit for the banquet of the King. As one of ours said, when he was condemned to the beasts for the testimony of God: 'I am the wheat of Christ, and I am ground by the teeth of the beasts, that I may be found the pure bread of God' (Ignatius, Romans 4:1). All things were made for the benefit of humanity; and the snares of the Antichrist, his wickedness, and apostate power were prefigured from the flood onward, and afterward in the persecution of Ananias, Azarias, and Misael (Dan 3).

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Latin text. Pass A provides a faithful literal rendering, and Pass B provides a fluent English version with appropriate scripture citations (e.g., Matt 25:34, 41; 2 Thess 2:10-12; Rev 13:1-18; Gen 2:1-2; Ps 90:4; Ignatius, Romans 4:1; Dan 3) that correspond to the content and allusions in the Latin. The title 'The Millennium' correctly identifies the central thought of the chapter regarding the 6,000-year period.
